title: heuchera rubescens var. versicolor
intro: Heuchera rubescens var. versicolor, commonly known as the Coral Bells, is a type of flowering plant in the saxifrage family (Saxifragaceae) that is native to the western United States. This plant is valued for its attractive foliage, with maple-like leaves in shades of coral, pink, and red, as well as its ability to attract pollinators. Heuchera rubescens var. versicolor has been traditionally used in herbal medicine for its health benefits, including reducing inflammation and improving digestion, and its therapeutic actions include anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects. The bioactive constituents of this plant include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and saponins, which contribute to its medicinal properties.
